chapter: Hollywood and the break with Thornhill
title: Songs of unusual form rather than 32-bar AABA
summary: She and Claude chose off-the-beaten-track songs that didn't become overworked.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: The other two songs are "Moments Like This" and "Please Be Kind." Both of them are of the ABAB structure --
Rather than the -- they -- more conventional, I think, AABA 32-bar chorus.
Probably at this period you sang more of these kinds of songs than the other. Did you have a preference for that form of song?

Yes.
Well, I'll tell you one of the things.
They're off the beaten track, you know. And I think between Claude and myself, we try to be selective in the material that we use.
We didn't want to -- well, we weren't trying to pick up on what was currently popular, trying to make the hit parade, or anything like that.
Because after having done "Loch Lomond," there wasn't anything that we could do to top it.
So we just spent the time trying to select the kind of
